extracted.intended_audience: federal agency managers, policymakers, oversight staff, and researchers interested in U.S. federal performance management
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and evaluative criteria for federal agencies to plan, measure, report, and improve program performance under the Government Performance and Results Act (1993) and the GPRA Modernization Act (2010). Focuses on strategic plans, annual performance plans and reports, indicators, verification, and related implementation provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-year strategic plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to develop five-year strategic plans that must contain a mission statement for the agency as well as long-term, results-oriented goals covering each of its major functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic plans should articulate mission and long-term, results-oriented goals across major functions; they are the foundational GPRA product that informs annual plans and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual performance plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to prepare annual performance plans that establish the performance goals for the applicable fiscal year, a brief description of how these goals are to be met, and a description of how these performance goals can be verified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual plans must set fiscal-year goals, describe strategies/actions to meet them, and specify verification methods (data sources, indicators, evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual performance reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must prepare annual performance reports that review the agency's success or failure in meeting its targeted performance goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should compare achieved performance to targets, explain successes/failures, and are sent to the President and Congress and made accessible to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance indicators / outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Each report includes a list of performance goals for each program. This includes indicators that help measure the outcome for each goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete indicators to measure outcomes for each goal and present results relative to the targets in plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation and corrective plan for unmet goals
rubrics_metrics.description: If the performance goal was not met for that fiscal year, an explanation has to be given for why the goals that were proposed were not met. Following up the explanation, they have to give a written plan of what they will do to meet their goals the following fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must include root-cause explanations for missed targets and a written remediation/follow-up plan describing actions for the next fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of performance goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual performance plans must include a description of how these performance goals can be verified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe verification methods (data, measurement approaches, validation) so stakeholders can assess whether reported performance is credible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of program activities in budget
rubrics_metrics.description: The performance goals must cover each program activity made in the agency budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure alignment between budgeted program activities and stated performance goals; every budget activity should be tied to measurable goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify key external factors beyond agency control
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to identify 'key factors external to the agency and beyond its control that could significantly affect the achievement of the general goals and objectives'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List external risks/conditions (economic, legal, environmental, interagency dependencies) that could impede goal achievement and discuss how they affect plans and targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish plans and reports in machine-readable formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 10 requires agencies to publish their strategic and performance plans and reports in machine-readable formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure electronic publication in machine-readable standards (the page cites StratML as an example) to facilitate transparency, data reuse, and automated oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: State operational processes, budgeting strategies, technology and skills, and other resources
rubrics_metrics.description: GPRA calls for agencies to clearly state their operational process, budgeting strategies, technology and skill positions, as well as other resources necessary to meeting goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the organizational capabilities and resource needs (human capital, IT, capital, information) required to achieve goals and how they will be marshaled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare current results to previous years
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare current results to previous years as a measure of effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use longitudinal comparison to assess progress over time and to contextualize annual performance results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct gap analyses and project planning
rubrics_metrics.description: To comply with the GPRA, agencies produce strategic plans, performance plans, and conduct gap analyses of projects; GPRA established project planning and strategic planning and set up a framework of reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gap analyses to identify discrepancies between current performance and goals, inform planning, and prioritize corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Management and Budget (OMB) reporting and executive oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Management and Budget is tasked pursuant to the GPRA with producing an annual report on agency performance. This is produced with the President's annual budget request. The Executive branch oversees the implementation of the GPRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should coordinate performance reporting with OMB requirements and understand that OMB/Executive oversight influences how plans and reports are reviewed and presented alongside budget submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public accessibility and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: These results will be sent to the President and to Congress. The results can be accessed by the public once they are published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure transparency: publish results publicly, enabling congressional oversight and public trust; reports should be understandable and accessible to external stakeholders.
